exposure: Hyperbaric bupivacaine (0.5%) with fentanyl (25 mcg) as adjuvant for spinal anaesthesia
Hyperbaric bupivacaine (0.5%) with neostigmine (25 mcg) as adjuvant for spinal anaesthesia
Hyperbaric bupivacaine (0.5%) with 0.5 ml normal saline as control for spinal anaesthesia
cohort: The study included 96 ASA I & II patients undergoing lower abdominal and lower extremity surgery at a tertiary care center in Lucknow.
finding: Neostigmine as an adjuvant to hyperbaric bupivacaine in spinal anaesthesia resulted in significantly higher mean pulse rate, lower bradycardia rates, and reduced need for rescue analgesia compared to fentanyl as an adjuvant or bupivacaine alone.
